original_question: Let X be a complex subvariety of the unit ball B with an isolated singularity at the origin. Suppose Omegat is a continuously increasing family of Stein open subsets of X. Also, suppose that 0 ∈ ∂Omega1/2 , 0 ∈ Omegat , t > 1/2. Is Omegas Runge in Omegat ∀s < t?
target_in_paper: The draft most likely targets the unnumbered Stein-space/Levi-problem item in arXiv:math/9509202 asking whether, for a continuously increasing family of Stein open sets on a singular complex space crossing an isolated singularity at the parameter value t = 1/2, the earlier domains are Runge in the later ones. The arXiv entry shows that math/9509202 is The Several Complex Variables Problem List, and later papers on the same Stein-space open-problem circle reproduce the distinctive phrases about an isolated singularity and a continuously increasing family of Stein open subsets. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9509202))
correct_elements: Your draft captures the core mathematical content correctly: the ambient object is a complex subvariety/space with an isolated singularity at 0; there is a nested one-parameter family {Ω_t} of Stein open subsets; the singular point lies on the boundary at t = 1/2 and is inside Ω_t for t > 1/2; and the question asks whether Ω_s is Runge in Ω_t for every s < t. That is very close to the recognizable open problem discussed in the Stein-space/Levi-problem context. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=ddcbe25077121277bed380761981c39a92aad464&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
missing_details: The parameter set for the family should be stated explicitly, typically as t in an interval such as [0,1], not left implicit. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=ddcbe25077121277bed380761981c39a92aad464&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

“Continuously increasing family” should be unpacked: at minimum, Ω_s ⊂ Ω_t for s < t, and the intended continuity with respect to t should be stated rather than assumed. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=ddcbe25077121277bed380761981c39a92aad464&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
The ambient ball should be identified as the unit ball B ⊂ C^n (or B ⊂ C^N), since “unit ball” without ambient dimension is not fully stand-alone. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9509202))

It should be explicit that the singularity is at the origin and isolated in X; if the source formulation follows the later summaries exactly, normality may also be intended and should then be stated. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=ddcbe25077121277bed380761981c39a92aad464&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The statement should specify that each Ω_t is an open Stein subset of X with its induced complex-space structure. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=ddcbe25077121277bed380761981c39a92aad464&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The quantifiers on s and t should be written explicitly: for all s,t in the parameter interval with s < t. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=ddcbe25077121277bed380761981c39a92aad464&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

If the question is meant to be fully self-contained, the meaning of “Ω_s is Runge in Ω_t” should be spelled out, since the paper title indicates a problem-list format rather than a theorem-proposition setup that would automatically fix conventions. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9509202))
refined_question: Let B ⊂ C^n be the unit ball, let X ⊂ B be a complex subvariety with an isolated singularity at 0, and let {Ω_t}_{0≤t≤1} be a continuously increasing family of Stein open subsets of X such that 0 ∈ ∂Ω_{1/2} and 0 ∈ Ω_t for every t > 1/2. Is it true that Ω_s is Runge in Ω_t for every 0 ≤ s < t ≤ 1? ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=ddcbe25077121277bed380761981c39a92aad464&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
justification: The arXiv item math/9509202 is not a standard theorem paper but a problem list, so the target here is an unnumbered open problem rather than a numbered conjecture/theorem. Your draft aligns closely with a recognizable Stein-space problem about increasing Stein families near an isolated singularity and pairwise Runge-ness. The later Levi-problem literature summarizes the same surrounding context—namely increasing unions of Stein open subsets on spaces with isolated singularities—and cites Colţoiu’s open-problems work in that exact area, while a separate search snippet preserves the distinctive wording about an isolated singularity and a continuously increasing family of Stein open subsets. Because the exact PDF text of the 1995 arXiv source was not directly retrievable in this browsing session, I kept the rewrite as close as possible to your draft while only sharpening the hidden quantifiers and ambient notation, and I did not add stronger hypotheses unless they were at least suggested by later summaries. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9509202))
